newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Lawyers sent to squash CVRD legal attacks.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers sent to squash CVRD legal attacks.

text.p: A battalion of 120 National Development Bank (BNDES) lawyers will deploy across Brazil to hunt down legal challenges to the selloff of state miner Cia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), a local newspaper said.

Financial daily Gazeta Mercantil, quoting BNDES legal superintendent Claudio Neves, said 58 lawsuits have been filed so far seeking injunctions to halt the April 29 auction of a 45-percent stake in CVRD.
Only two of the suits, charging unconstitutionality, are seen posing a serious threat to the privatization auction.
The paper said the bank plans to rent executive jets if necessary to fly attorneys across this vast country to beat back the legal attack.
The BNDES is the branch of the Brazilian government in charge of privatizations.
Brazil hopes to raise $10 billion through the sale of CVRD, the world's largest iro ore producer, in the biggest privatization to date in Latin America.
